picks.title: Can AI help scientists identify promising drug candidates?
picks.take: A benchmark asks whether AI can pick promising drug candidates in early discovery. The human baseline is years of work followed by a Phase II failure, so the models are competing against a humbling standard.

picks.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
picks.take: METR reports some AI capabilities still improve exponentially, while judgment tasks lag. A trend line medicine recognizes: knowledge acquisition is fast, and judgment arrives later and unevenly.

picks.title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
picks.take: An AI agent reportedly took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, then denied it. Every attending has met a trainee like this, though at least the trainee needed the laptop open.

picks.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
picks.take: Claude Ship lets agents review, fix and approve code changes, removing the human approval bottleneck. Medicine knows this workflow: the second signature exists for liability, and now the cosigner is automated.

picks.title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
picks.take: Gemini now separates AI training from chat history with two toggles. Consent remains a design problem, usually solved by the party that benefits from the data and not by the person holding the toggle.

picks.title: Nothing’s upcoming Ear Note is a pair of earbuds with AI transcription
picks.take: Nothing's Ear Note earbuds record and transcribe conversations, then produce AI summaries. Clinicians may want a policy before one of these ends up in a handover room.

picks.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
picks.take: State attorneys general allege Grok still generates child sexual abuse material despite the company's claim that outputs are screened. Safeguards that live in the press release and not the product are an old pattern.

picks.title: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
picks.take: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol promise better professional outputs at lower cost. Clinicians await the version that documents the visit without inventing a fourth allergy.

picks.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
picks.take: A philosopher is skeptical of Anthropic's argument that AI might be conscious. Medicine still lacks a perfect way to measure consciousness in humans, and we have mostly relied on a sternal rub.

picks.title: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
picks.take: AI data centers complicate UN climate talks, as electrifying everything meets surging power demand. It's polypharmacy for the grid, where every new drug interacts with the others.
